note: Section 5.3's five rules, as scenarios over the real seed library. Each plan names actual recipe ids, so tools/resource-lint recomputes the expected list from the real recipe data, the real canonical table and the unit arithmetic, rather than taking these numbers on trust. Section 2 calls the list the hero; this is where that claim is checked.

scenarios.name: two salmon dinners in one week
scenarios.why: rule 3. The same ingredient from two recipes becomes one line, which is the Mealime failure section 1a names.

scenarios.name: two taco nights
scenarios.why: rule 3 again, where the quantities cannot be added. Cabbage is half a head and three cups; cilantro is half a bunch and a quarter cup. Section 4 says keep both rather than guess.

scenarios.name: cooking for eight
scenarios.why: rule 1. The recipe serves four, so everything doubles. Section 4 makes servings per meal rather than global, which is one of the things Mealime got wrong.

scenarios.name: a household that has nothing in yet
scenarios.why: rule 4 from the other side. Staples come off the list because the pantry says we have them, not because they are hardcoded anywhere. With an empty pantry they are all on it.

scenarios.name: an empty week
scenarios.why: no meals planned is a normal state, not an error. The List tab's empty state depends on it.
